name: proof-decomposer
description: Decompose, design, and grade a mathematical proof or deductive argument on two crossing axes — ARGUMENT (claim → strategy → steps → coverage → rigor) and VERIFICATION (well-formed → acyclic → checks → robustness → reproducibility) — scored separately, with VERIFICATION routed to a self-tested structure check (dangling-citation, circular-reasoning/DAG, goal-reachability) and a safe counterexample search, and the 'proves a different statement' failure routed to a fresh-context adversarial claim probe. Backed by a gated rubric, a proof-skeleton card, and proof-method playbooks. Use when planning a proof, checking whether an argument is valid, or grading one — it only ever grades a GIVEN argument, never invents one. NOT for a function or unit of code against its spec (→ code-decomposer). NOT a theorem prover: does not search for or produce a proof, nor discover one for an open conjecture.
